html:
The Azande are a people of north central Africa, living today where South Sudan, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the Central African Republic meet. The map uses their name, in its 900 snapshot, for a wide belt of savanna from the Ubangi River to the upper Nile, centuries before the Azande existed as a people.

In 900 this land held farming villages whose people spoke Ubangian and Central Sudanic languages, without large states that we know of.

The Azande took shape in the 1700s, when the ruling Avongara clan led conquests that joined many peoples under Zande rule. By the 1800s their kingdoms traded ivory with merchants from Sudan and fought off slave raiders. The anthropologist E. E. Evans-Pritchard made them famous with his study of their ideas of witchcraft and oracles.
